sowhat.text: Mega-deals keep getting signed, from CrowdStrike's all-stock Zscaler bid to Sanofi's cash offer for Insmed, and the Lukoil sale shows energy M&A now runs through sanctions approvals. With core PCE at 3.3% and the 10-year at 4.85%, debt-funded buyers face a high base rate, which favors stock deals and strategic buyers.

pitch: Markets were choppy going into Thanksgiving. Stocks sold off hard on tariff headlines and an AI-chip rout, then recovered, so the S&P 500 closed at about 7,180, down a quarter of a percent. Core inflation came in hot at 3.3%, yet the 10-year fell 6 bp to about 4.85%, and the Fed sits at 3.75 to 4% with a meeting on 8 and 9 December. Oil bounced, with WTI near $84 and Brent near $95. On deals, CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $44 billion in stock and Sanofi is buying Insmed for $41 billion in cash, so large strategic deals are getting done even with rates this high.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury close on Wed 25 Nov?
Why was the S&P 500 down only 0.3% on 25 Nov after being down about 3% at its low?
quiz.a: The tariff and AI-chip sell-off faded and buyers stepped in, so stocks recovered most of the morning losses.

quiz.q: Who is acquiring Zscaler, and how is the roughly $43.9B deal being paid for?
quiz.a: CrowdStrike, in an all-stock deal at 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

chat.q: What's your read on rates right now?
chat.a: The 10-year closed at 4.85%, down 6 bp, even though core PCE ran at 3.3%, above the 3.2% expected. The Fed funds range is 3.75–4.00% after a hike in September, and the next FOMC is 8-9 December. For deals, a high base rate makes leveraged buyouts harder to finance and favors strategics paying in stock or cash.
chat.tip: Lead with the 10-year, then tie it to financing.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $83.68, up 2.0%, and Brent at $94.61, up 3.5%, a spread of about $11. Higher crude supports upstream cash flow and energy deal appetite, but adds to the inflation pressure the Fed is watching.
chat.tip: Name both benchmarks and the spread.

chat.a: CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler for about $43.9B in stock, advised by Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and BofA for CrowdStrike and BDT & MSD, Citi and Goldman for Zscaler. Sanofi is buying Insmed for about $41.0B in cash. Both show large strategic deals proceeding despite a 4.85% 10-year.

chat.q: Why did stocks recover from a big drop on Wednesday?
chat.a: The S&P 500 was down 3.2% at its low after tariff reports and an AI-chip sell-off, then closed down only 0.3% at 7,183. The VIX closed at 28.29, still elevated. Volatility like this can delay IPO and financing launches until conditions settle.
chat.tip: Show you know the intraday swing, not just the close.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: A higher risk-free rate raises the discount rate, so present value falls, most for long-duration cash flows and terminal value. From today's 4.85% that would mean about 5.35%. Highly levered buyers would also see financing costs rise, pressuring LBO returns.
chat.tip: Walk through the WACC mechanics first.

chat.q: Walk me through how an all-stock deal like CrowdStrike and Zscaler works.
chat.a: Each Zscaler share converts to 1.135 CrowdStrike shares, valuing Zscaler at about $43.9B enterprise value, a roughly 34% premium. CrowdStrike holders would own about 84.1% of the combined company. All-stock avoids new debt at a 4.85% 10-year, but exposes both sides to CrowdStrike's share price until closing.
chat.tip: Cover premium, exchange ratio and ownership split.

chat.q: Why might energy M&A run through sanctions approvals, as in the Lukoil sale?
chat.a: The Eldridge-led consortium would swap restricted Russian shares for 100% of LUKOIL International, which has about 350,000 boe/d of upstream output and three refineries. It needs conditional OFAC approval, so regulatory structure matters as much as price. With Brent at $94.61, the assets are valuable, but closing certainty drives the timeline.
chat.tip: Frame it as deal certainty versus valuation.
